subject: science

concepts.title: Classification of Natural Resources
concepts.definition: Sorting materials extracted from nature into inexhaustible categories available in limitless quantities and exhaustible categories reduced through continuous human consumption.
concepts.key_idea: Natural materials are grouped into infinite supply sources and depletable supply sources based on human usage impact.
question_patterns: classify natural resources as inexhaustible or exhaustible in Class 8 science
what is the difference between exhaustible and inexhaustible resources
give examples of inexhaustible natural resources in nature
why are forests and minerals considered exhaustible resources
how are natural materials grouped according to their availability

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the given resource exists in unlimited or limited quantity in nature.
If human activity leads to depletion, classify as exhaustible; if not, classify as inexhaustible.
Confirm the classification by citing examples: sunlight and air are inexhaustible while coal, petroleum, and forests are exhaustible.

concepts.title: Coal and Carbonisation
concepts.definition: A dark solid fossil fuel formed over subterranean geological epochs through the slow breakdown of buried dense vegetation under elevated subterranean temperature and pressure.
concepts.key_idea: The slow chemical transformation of dead plant remnants into carbon-enriched material is termed carbonisation.
question_patterns: explain the process of coal formation from dead vegetation in Class 8 science
what is carbonisation in Class 8 coal and petroleum
describe why coal is classified as a fossil fuel
how did ancient forests transform into coal deposits underground
what physical conditions turn dead plant matter into coal

solution_steps.explain: Wetland forests became covered under layers of soil due to natural events like flooding.
Deeper burial caused extreme pressure and temperature increases in the absence of air.
The slow chemical change converting dead plant matter into carbon is carbonisation.

concepts.title: Products of Coal: Coke, Coal Tar, and Coal Gas
concepts.definition: Destructive distillation of raw coal in industry isolates a solid porous carbon residue (coke), a viscous liquid mixture (coal tar), and a combustible gaseous mixture (coal gas).
concepts.key_idea: Industrial processing of coal yields coke for metallurgy, coal tar for chemical synthesis, and coal gas for heating.
question_patterns: what are the main products obtained from coal processing in Class 8 science
describe the characteristics and industrial uses of coke
what is coal tar and list key products manufactured from it
how is coal gas formed and utilized in industries
compare coke, coal tar, and coal gas based on physical state and application

solution_steps.explain: Coke is black, porous, tough, and nearly pure carbon used in steel manufacturing and metal extraction.
Coal tar is a foul-smelling dark liquid containing around 200 substances used for dyes, drugs, and explosives.
Coal gas evolves during coke production and serves as an industrial heat source.

concepts.title: Formation and Origin of Petroleum
concepts.definition: A naturally occurring liquid fossil fuel created from ancient sea organisms buried beneath silt, transformed over millions of years without air under intense heat and pressure.
concepts.key_idea: Petroleum and natural gas accumulate beneath impermeable rock strata above water layers because they are lighter than water.
question_patterns: how is crude petroleum formed under marine ocean beds
explain why crude oil and natural gas sit above water in underground deposits
where was the world's first oil well drilled and where was oil found in India
describe the marine origin of petroleum in Class 8 science
what environmental conditions convert ancient aquatic organisms into crude oil

solution_steps.explain: Dead sea organisms settle on the sea floor and get covered by clay and sand layers.
Anaerobic environment combined with high pressure and temperature converts organic remains into oil and gas.
Oil and gas float above groundwater deposits due to lower density and immiscibility.

concepts.title: Petroleum Refining and Components
concepts.definition: Industrial separation of complex dark crude petroleum into marketable fractions such as petrol, diesel, kerosene, lubricating oil, and paraffin wax.
concepts.key_idea: Refining splits crude oil into distinct useful constituents inside specialized petroleum refineries.
question_patterns: what is petroleum refining and where is the process conducted
list key constituents of petroleum and their corresponding uses
which petroleum fraction is used for road surfacing in modern roads
what fuel powers heavy transport vehicles and electric generators
how are kerosene and paraffin wax derived from crude petroleum

solution_steps.explain: Refining isolates individual hydrocarbon components from crude oil based on property differences.
Petrol fuels light vehicles, diesel runs heavy machinery, jet engines use kerosene, bitumen surfaces roads.
Each fraction is separated by differences in boiling point and density, confirming the correct industrial use of the constituent.

concepts.title: Petrochemicals and Black Gold
concepts.definition: Chemical compounds derived from crude oil or natural gas utilized to synthesize commercial polymers, synthetic fibers, detergents, and agricultural fertilizers.
concepts.key_idea: Petroleum earns the nickname black gold due to its massive commercial significance across multiple industries.
question_patterns: what are petrochemicals and state their commercial applications
why is petroleum referred to as black gold in Class 8 science
which gas produced from natural gas is essential for chemical fertilizers
name synthetic materials manufactured using petrochemical feedstocks
explain the economic importance of petroleum products in everyday life

solution_steps.explain: Useful chemical compounds extracted from natural gas and crude petroleum are called petrochemicals.
They yield plastics, polyester, nylon, detergents, and hydrogen gas for urea production.
The term reflects the supreme monetary and industrial value of dark crude oil.

concepts.title: Natural Gas and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)
concepts.definition: A non-polluting gaseous fossil fuel found alongside petroleum deposits, stored under elevated pressure as CNG for pipe delivery and clean vehicular combustion.
concepts.key_idea: Natural gas stored as CNG is a clean-burning fuel distributed through pipeline networks directly to consumers.
question_patterns: what are the main advantages of using CNG as a fuel
why is natural gas considered a cleaner fuel than petrol or diesel
where are natural gas reserves located within India
how is compressed natural gas transported to homes and factories
what makes CNG suitable for power generation and vehicles

solution_steps.explain: Natural gas compressed at high pressure forms CNG, which can be safely stored and piped.
CNG burns completely with minimal smoke, reducing atmospheric pollution.
Reserves exist in Tripura, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and Krishna Godavari delta.

concepts.title: Conservation of Natural Resources and PCRA Guidelines
concepts.definition: Strategies designed to curtail fuel consumption, extend finite fossil fuel reserves, and mitigate environmental issues like air pollution and global warming.
concepts.key_idea: Judicious driving habits recommended by PCRA reduce fuel wastage and environmental pollution.
question_patterns: why must fossil fuels be used judiciously in Class 8 science
what fuel-saving tips are recommended by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association
how does burning fossil fuels contribute to global warming and pollution
what practical measures reduce petrol and diesel consumption while driving
explain why fossil fuels cannot be synthesized artificially in laboratories

solution_steps.explain: Fossil fuels require geological timescales to form and cannot be produced in laboratories.
Maintain steady moderate speed, switch off engine at traffic signals, maintain correct tyre pressure and regular servicing.
Reduced fuel consumption lowers carbon emissions, mitigating air pollution and global warming while extending finite reserves.

concepts.title: Power Shortage Percentage Difference Calculation
concepts.definition: Quantitative comparison of power deficit percentages across distinct recording years to evaluate supply-demand trends.
concepts.key_idea: The algebraic difference between shortage percentages measures the change in energy deficit over time.
question_patterns: calculate the difference in power shortage percentage between two years
find the change in power shortage percentage from year1 to year2
compute the increase or decrease in power shortage percentage
determine the net change in shortage percentage over a given period
calculate how much power shortage percentage changed between given years

solution_steps.explain: subtract initial year shortage percentage from final year shortage percentage
a positive value indicates an increase in shortage while a negative value indicates a decrease
state the absolute change in percentage points to quantify the shift in power deficit

concepts.title: Remaining Fuel Reserve Percentage Calculation
concepts.definition: Computing the unconsumed fraction of a limited fuel reserve relative to its initial total capacity.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting consumed resource from total capacity gives remaining stock, expressed as a percentage of the total.
question_patterns: calculate the percentage of fuel reserve remaining after consumption
find the remaining percentage of a coal reserve given initial and consumed amounts
compute the percent of natural gas reserve left in stock
determine the remaining fuel percentage from total and used quantities
calculate how much percentage of a petroleum reserve is left

solution_steps.explain: subtract consumed fuel from total reserve
divide remaining amount by total reserve and multiply by 100
confirm that remaining percentage plus consumed percentage equals 100 percent of the total reserve

worked_examples.question_pattern: In India, the power shortage was {shortage_year1}% in 1991 and {shortage_year2}% in 1997. Calculate the difference in power shortage percentage.

solution_template.explain: subtract initial year shortage percentage from final year shortage percentage

worked_examples.question_pattern: The power shortage percentage was {shortage_year1}% in 1993 and {shortage_year2}% in 1995. Find the change in shortage percentage.

solution_template.explain: subtract initial year shortage percentage from final year shortage percentage

worked_examples.question_pattern: A coal mine has a total reserve of {total_reserve} million tonnes. If {consumed_amount} million tonnes have been extracted, calculate the percentage of reserve remaining.

solution_template.explain: subtract consumed fuel from total reserve
divide remaining amount by total reserve and multiply by 100

worked_examples.question_pattern: A petroleum field had {total_reserve} thousand barrels of oil. After consuming {consumed_amount} thousand barrels, find the remaining percentage of oil.

solution_template.explain: subtract consumed fuel from total reserve
divide remaining amount by total reserve and multiply by 100
